variables.name: Land surface air temperature
variables.source: NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 (GHCNv4 land stations), anomalies vs 1951-1980
variables.about: Average temperature of the air near the ground over land, shown as change from a long-term average. Land only: GISTEMP over oceans is the same data as sea surface temperature, so including it would double count.

variables.name: Precipitation
variables.source: GPCP v2.3 monthly (NOAA PSL), 2.5° regridded to 2°
variables.about: Rain and snow reaching the ground, combining satellites and rain gauges. Trends can be wetter in one place and drier in another.

variables.name: Sea surface temperature
variables.about: Temperature of the top layer of the ocean. Drives weather, storms and marine ecosystems.

method.trend: Seasonal cycle removed; slope = least-squares rate per year; significance = Mann-Kendall test.
method.combined: Each variable's |Mann-Kendall Z| is converted to a percentile rank (0-1) so units don't matter; the combined score is the mean over variables with data in that cell (>= 2 required). Variables are restricted to where they are measured independently (temperature = land, sea surface temperature = ocean) so nothing is counted twice.
method.interpolation: Holes of up to 4 grid cells that are surrounded by data are filled by inverse-distance weighting of nearby cells. Larger gaps (poles, sea ice, no coverage) are never filled. Filled cells are marked as interpolated, and can be hidden with 'Observed data only'.
